preamble: The diphthong [au] is reduced to the monophthong [a] by two different routes. In West Greenlandic, Proto-Inuit vowel sequences coalesced into long vowels, so *au became [aː] (ataaseq 'one' beside Inuktitut atausiq), and East Greenlandic shares the outcome. In Latin, /au̯/ dissimilated to /a/ when the next syllable contained /u/: nonstandard agustus for augustus (attested from the 1st century CE) and ascultō for auscultō (2nd century CE) are the bases of Italian and Spanish agosto and Italian ascoltare.

examples.note: cf. Inuktitut atausiq; East Greenlandic (Tunumiisut) alaasiq also has aa
cf. Inuktitut uqausiq; East Greenlandic oraasiq

examples.to: agustus (nonstandard, attested from the mid–late 1st century CE)
examples.note: Dissimilation of /au̯/ before a following /u/; continued in Italian and Spanish agosto, Romanian agust.
Same dissimilation before the /u/ of the next syllable; continued in Italian ascoltare.
